source: Genomic Surveillance of Climate-Amplified Cholera Outbreak Malawi 2022-2023
processing_notes: Source states: 'After the initial 1973 introduction, Malawi experienced significant cholera activity in 1975, reporting as many as 22,427 cases in that single year, which represents one of the highest case counts in the country's cholera history' - interpreted as 22427 sCh cases
retracted_reason: Retracted as unsupportable on two independent grounds. (1) MISATTRIBUTION: the row cites metadata Index 11 (EID 31(6) 'Genomic Surveillance of Climate-Amplified Cholera Outbreak, Malawi, 2022-2023'); direct retrieval of that article shows it contains no 1970s case counts at all - its only pre-1998 statement is 'In Malawi, cholera was first reported in 1973'. The quote stored in processing_notes does not appear in the cited source. The 22,427/1975 figure actually originates in Kachimanga et al., PLOS Global Public Health 2025, 'Determinants of cholera fatalities in Malawi'. (2) CONTRADICTED BY THE PRIMARY RECORD: WHO WER 51(18), 30 April 1976, Table 1 'Cases of Cholera Notified to WHO, 1975' enumerates every African country that notified cholera in 1975 - Algeria 16, Angola 88, Benin 29, Cape Verde 20, Comoros 2675, Ghana 170, Kenya 1093, Liberia 704, Mozambique 11, Nigeria 156, Southern Rhodesia 615, Uganda 31, United Rep. of Cameroon 3, Upper Volta 3, Africa TOTAL 5,586 - and Malawi is not among them. The entire African continent notified fewer than a quarter of the cases this row attributes to Malawi alone. Independently reproduced by CDC MMWR 25(27), 16 July 1976, Table 2. WHO GHO CHOLERA_0000000001 likewise has no 1975 entry for Malawi. Superseded by a Documented_Absence row for 1975 sourced to WER 51(18).

source: Cholera-free period validation 1976-1987 Malawi surveillance WHO academic
processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission during 1976-1987 - validated absence via multiple academic sources documenting gap between 1975 major outbreak (22,427 cases) and 1988 refugee camp outbreak (951 cases). Surveillance system was functioning as it detected 1988 outbreak.
retracted_reason: Retracted: this row asserts sCh=0, deaths=0 for the whole of 1976-01-01..1987-12-31, and WHO's own record contradicts it for five years inside that window. WHO GHO indicator CHOLERA_0000000001 for Malawi gives 1976=19, 1977=577, 1978=263, 1981=261, 1983=487 cases (with 1978=24 and 1983=49 deaths), and the identical values are already present in the JHU baseline ./data/MWI/cholera_data_jhu.csv Index 1229-1233. WER 60(20) 'Cholera in 1984' further describes Malawi as one of the countries that 'experienced large outbreaks in 1983'. The row's stated rationale - an uninterrupted gap between a 1975 outbreak and the 1988 refugee-camp outbreak - is doubly wrong: the 1975 outbreak it is anchored to never happened (see retracted Index 12), and the 1976-1987 window was not cholera-free. Because py/build_weekly_timeseries.py renders a documented zero as sCh=0, leaving this row in place would have written twelve years of false negatives, five of them over years WHO recorded hundreds of cases. Replaced by year-resolved rows sourced to the individual WER annual reviews: 1975, 1979, 1980, 1985 and 1986 are added as Documented_Absence; 1976-1978, 1981 and 1983 are already carried by the JHU baseline; 1982, 1984 and 1987 are left genuinely open because the WER issues for those years either carry no country table or are ambiguous.
